notes: All 53 beads read in full and every dependency judged (413 edges, 392 real). Shape: the C2 segment is mostly genuine work in sequence (Habitat scene compiler, sensors, estimator, Spark determinism), held on the chain by a few edges that name a consumer, a duplicate check or a record owned elsewhere. Applying all 21 proposals together (splits modelled as new nodes) takes the longest chain from 169 to 155; the C2 beads drop as follows: N37-23 66 to 27, BD-126 71 to 60, BD-162 86 to 23, BD-163 93 to 71, BD-166 96 to 81, BD-219 101 to 90, N16b-02 106 to 93, BD-177 110 to 93, BD-181 116 to 89, BD-186 118 to 103. The new chain still passes through BD-109 (by N18b-02, then ROBOT-anymal-b and the batched step) and through N38a-20 > N16b-02 > BD-212, so the next audit should look at N38a-20's and N18b-02's inbound edges. The chain has many parallel paths of equal length, so a single fix often moves only its own bead and descendants; gains are stated per bead for that reason. No start-ready bead was found: every bead of the list has at least one real dependency above level 20. Gaps found while judging, not proposals: the template four-point-stance@1 that BD-126's fixtures use has no owner; N25b-01 in frob-core uses frob-spec's Binder and Horizon types (a layering question); the 'provisional envelope' of N35-09's boundary flag is computed by no bead; N36-19's item 5 checks a time estimate it does not depend on; BD-160's cancel step duplicates N16a-18 step 15. Edges added inside proposals: BD-097 on N37-23; BD-126 on N25a-01; N14b-24 on the new URDF-rows bead; N36-32 on BD-188; N32a-15 on N32a-16; N35-09 on N35-04 and BD-208; N21b-42 on N21c-30.
